  "concordance_definition": "Likelihood Ratios (LRs) are used to measure the evidential weight provided by a test in one species for or against the toxicity of a given compound in another species. A PLR/iNLR statistically significantly higher than 1.0 indicates the animal species contributes some degree of evidential weight.",
  "limitations_stated": [
    "Data set is affected by selection bias/effect, as highly toxic drugs in rodents are unlikely to advance to tests in dogs, NHPs, and humans, leading to under-representation.",
    "The precautionary principle is an inherent aspect of the testing protocol, making it virtually impossible to gauge the actual contribution of animal data to human toxicology.",
    "A large proportion of the data reflected adverse events that are rare, potentially compromising reliability.",
    "Low numbers of observations in one or more species for NHP-human pair.",
    "Difficulty in accessing NHP toxicology data, with little publicly available.",
    "High ranges of PLRs with no obvious pattern of toxicity suggest reliability cannot be generalised or regarded with confidence.",
    "Use of a different total data set for NHP iNLR may account for it being the lowest.",
    "Analyses are necessarily based on relatively limited publicly-available data."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": null,
  "key_numbers": [
    "Over 3,000 drugs with both animal and human data were analyzed.",
    "Absence of toxicity in animals provides little or virtually no evidential weight for absence of toxicity in humans.",
    "Toxicity in one species may sometimes add evidential weight for risk of toxicity in another, but LRs are extremely inconsistent.",
    "NHP-human PLR values are among the lowest for PLRs and the lowest for iNLRs.",
    "Median iNLRs were substantially lower than PLRs, supporting the view that absence of toxicity in one species provides essentially no evidential weight for lack of toxicity in any other species.",
    "Hypothetical rat-rat PLR was 898; dog-dog PLR was 845.",
    "Hypothetical rat-rat iNLR was 17.3; dog-dog iNLR was 6.6.",
    "Tests in all five preclinical species (dogs, mice, NHPs, rabbits, rats) provide little to no evidential weight for predicting lack of toxicity in humans.",
    "Median iNLR for NHPs is the lowest of all five preclinical species.",
    "Poor iNLRs mean that toxic compounds are progressing to testing in humans, only to fail in clinical trials or soon after approval."
  ]
